variants.title: Budget independent shards
variants.context: A shard owns part of the data. With perfectly even traffic and no coordination cost, total capacity is the sum of shard capacities.
variants.prompt: Evenly distributed traffic is 950 requests/second. Each independent shard can sustain 300. What is the minimum whole number of shards?
variants.hint: Divide and round up. The even-distribution assumption matters.
variants.explanation: Round 950/300 upward to 4; an incomplete shard cannot serve traffic.

variants.title: Handle uneven traffic
variants.context: A hot shard receives more work than its peers. Total spare capacity elsewhere may not help its owner.
variants.prompt: One tenant owns 80% of traffic and all its records live on one shard. Adding unrelated empty shards leaves it overloaded. What should you examine?
options: How that tenant’s keys can be distributed or its traffic controlled.
Add empty shards without moving this tenant’s keys.
Raise the client timeout while keeping the same capacity.
variants.hint: Find who owns the busy data and how requests reach it.
variants.explanation: The hot ownership boundary must change or its load must fall.
optionFeedback: The hot ownership boundary must change or its load must fall.
